about.title: Engineered for Privacy. Built for Developers.
about.subtitle: A modern privacy-first developer utility suite. Engineered for instant, 100% client-side data parsing, formatting, and cryptographic operations with zero server network latency.
about.brandSectionDesc: The name isn't random. Every part of it describes exactly what developers go through, and what this platform was built around.
about.brandC3Desc: The superscript ³ stands for the three things every developer actually does every day. You write code. Something breaks. You spend hours reading cryptic stack traces, question every decision you made, and eventually fix it. Then you ship. That loop is the job. C³ MindLoop exists because that reality deserves to be named, not dressed up.
about.brandMindTitle: The loop inside your head that never shuts off.
about.brandMindDesc: You're in the shower thinking about a race condition. You wake up at 3am knowing exactly why the client-side JSON Formatter was throwing on nested nulls. That's the developer mind, always running, always iterating. MindLoop is that cycle: Think, Build, Learn, Repeat. Not a motivational poster. Just what actually happens when you care about your craft.
about.brandLoopTitle: It never stops. That's the point.
about.brandLoopDesc: There's no finish line in software. Every shipped feature opens three more problems. Every solved bug teaches you something that changes how you write the next function. Whether you're building a client-side Base64 Encoder or a distributed auth system, the loop is the work. The faster you get at running it, the better your software gets.
about.brandPrivacyTitle: 100% Local Browser Execution. Zero Server Data Logging.
about.brandPrivacyDesc: Every private browser utility on this platform, including the client-side JSON Formatter, JWT Decoder, and Base64 Encoder, runs entirely in your browser. No data leaves your machine. No server logs your input. We built it this way because that's the only way we'd want to use it ourselves.
about.storyP1: C³ MindLoop is built to solve developer friction with absolute privacy. We deliver zero-latency client-side processing, seamless WebCrypto integration, and zero-log developer workflows.
about.storyP2: By running everything locally inside your browser tab, we protect your configurations, API keys, credentials, and codebases from being stored or tracked on remote networks.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about C³ MindLoop, our products, and community.
faq.q1: What does C³ MindLoop stand for?
faq.a1: C³ stands for Coding, Crashing, Crying-the actual loop every developer lives through daily. You write code, it breaks, you debug it, you ship. The superscript ³ is the honest shorthand for that cycle. MindLoop is the mental process that never fully switches off-you're in the shower thinking about a race condition, or waking up at 3am knowing why the null check failed. This platform is built around that developer reality, not a polished version of it.
faq.q2: What kind of tools does C³ MindLoop offer?
faq.a2: All tools run 100% locally in your browser-no account, no backend, no data collection. The current lineup: JSON Formatter, JWT Inspector, Base64 Encoder, Regex Tester, Cron Visualizer, cURL Converter, SQL to JSON Converter, Hash Generator, and ATS Resume Generator. There's also an Office Editor VS Code extension with 14,400+ marketplace installs. Every tool processes your data inside your browser tab. Nothing leaves your machine.
faq.q3: How do I get started with the tools?
faq.a3: Go to the Tools page and pick one. No signup, no install, no waiting. Paste your JSON, JWT, Base64 string, or regex pattern directly into the editor and results appear instantly. Each tool is a standalone browser utility you can bookmark and return to anytime. If you're trying a few for the first time, the JSON Formatter and JWT Inspector are the most used. The ATS Resume Generator is useful if you're actively job hunting as a developer.
faq.q4: Are C³ MindLoop open-source projects free to use?
faq.a4: Yes-all public repositories are open-source under the MIT license, meaning you can use, fork, modify, and distribute them for personal or commercial projects without restrictions. The browser tools are free with no paywalls or usage limits. The VS Code Office Editor extension is also free on the Visual Studio Marketplace with no premium tier. Browse the GitHub repository for source code, contribution guidelines, and open issues.
faq.q5: How can I get involved in the community?
faq.a5: The most direct path is GitHub-open issues, submit pull requests, or explore the source code. The community page lists active discussion channels. If you've had a painful production incident worth sharing, crash story submissions are welcome: real debugging postmortems, not polished case studies. Engineering guides on the site come from actual development work. If you've got something worth writing up, reach out through the contact page.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.heroSubtitle: At C³ MindLoop, data privacy is not an afterthought. It is built into our core architecture. Learn how our local-first browser execution protects your code and credentials.
privacy.section1Body: Unlike traditional developer utility websites that send your input data to remote servers via network calls, C³ MindLoop executes all processing directly inside your local web browser. Whether you are formatting complex JSON, decoding JWT authorization tokens, converting Base64 strings, or evaluating Regex patterns, every operation relies exclusively on your device's native browser engines, such as Web APIs and JavaScript runtimes. No payload, raw code, API key, or credential ever leaves your browser or gets transmitted across the internet.
privacy.section2Title: 2. Zero Data Collection, Retention, and Logging
privacy.section2Body: We operate under a strict Zero Data Retention policy. We do not store, log, monitor, inspect, or backup any data that you paste, type, or process within our tools. Because all processing happens offline on your client machine, we have zero access to your internal payloads, proprietary source code, or confidential tokens. There is no server-side database receiving your input. There never was.
privacy.section3Title: 3. Local Storage and Browser State Management
privacy.section3Body: To provide a seamless experience, such as remembering your active workspace settings, UI preferences, or temporary tool history, C³ MindLoop may use local browser storage mechanisms like localStorage and sessionStorage. This data lives strictly on your local machine. It is never transmitted to us or any third party, and you can clear it completely at any time through your browser settings.
privacy.section4Body: C³ MindLoop is designed to be completely ad-free and tracking-light. We do not use third-party advertising networks, cross-site trackers, or invasive data-mining cookies. Anonymous page view metrics are collected via Google Analytics 4 (GA4) with IP anonymization enabled (anonymize_ip: true), ensuring zero personal identifier collection. These metrics contain zero payload data and are used solely to monitor system performance and aggregate traffic trends.
privacy.section5Title: 5. Outgoing Client Requests and API Testing
privacy.section5Body: If you use our API and cURL testing utilities to trigger HTTP or REST requests, those requests originate directly from your web browser to your targeted destination endpoint. C³ MindLoop does not proxy, inspect, reroute, or log your API request bodies or headers. The connection is yours, end to end.
privacy.section6Body: C³ MindLoop incorporates verified open-source software libraries to handle specific formatting and parsing functions. These libraries run strictly inside your local browser environment and have no network access to external servers. We periodically review open-source components to ensure compliance with security standards and licensing requirements.
privacy.section7Body: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect architecture upgrades or new browser capabilities. Continued use of C³ MindLoop implies acceptance of the current policy. If you have questions about our client-side architecture or want to inspect how the tools work, feel free to reach out or browse our codebase on GitHub.
privacy.complianceBody: C³ MindLoop operates on a zero-server-retention architecture. Because no personally identifiable information (PII) is stored, tracked, or resold, our platform is fully compliant with EU GDPR and California CCPA guidelines by design.
privacy.footerEnd: or inspect our source on GitHub.

guide.title: How to Use This Online JSON Formatter & Beautifier
guide.intro: This free online JSON parser and beautifier gives you instant formatting, validation, minification, and tree-mapping for any JSON data. Here is the step-by-step technical process:
guide.step1: Input Paste/Load: Paste your raw, compressed, or unformatted JSON string into the left input panel, or click the sample button to load a standard structured dataset.
guide.step2: Lexical Parsing: The browser's native JSON parser tokenizes the input, confirming every character complies with standard array, object, string, number, and boolean notation (JSON lint pass).
guide.step3: Validation Check: The online JSON validator checks structural integrity. If issues are found, the output panel highlights the exact line location and description of the syntax mismatch.
guide.step4: Pretty Print & Tree Render: The beautified, pretty-printed result renders immediately in the right panel with your chosen spacing. Switch to the JSON explorer tree view for collapsible node navigation.
guide.privacyTitle: Why a Private, Client-Side JSON Viewer Matters
guide.privacyIntro: Many developers use cloud-based online JSON formatters that silently transmit payloads to remote servers. This creates real security risks. C³ MindLoop is a 100% browser-based JSON viewer — your data never leaves your machine:
guide.privacyBullet1: Zero Network Overhead: All JSON beautifying, linting, and minification runs inside your local browser context. It works fully offline once the page loads.
guide.privacyBullet2: Private Configuration Auditing: Sensitive data like database credentials, REST API tokens, and secret keys stay entirely on your device, eliminating the risk of server-side data leaks or log extraction.

faq.q1: What is a JSON Formatter and Beautifier?
faq.a1: A JSON formatter (also called a JSON beautifier or pretty printer) takes raw, minified, or unformatted JSON strings and converts them into human-readable output with proper indentation and line breaks. This online JSON formatter also validates your data against the JSON spec, making it the best JSON validator online for developers who need instant feedback without leaving the browser.
faq.q2: Is this JSON Formatter safe for sensitive corporate configs and API keys?
faq.a2: Yes, 100%. Unlike cloud-based online JSON formatters, C³ MindLoop is a fully client-side JSON viewer — it runs entirely in your browser's V8 engine. No data is ever uploaded, stored, or logged on any server. Your API keys, database credentials, and proprietary payloads stay strictly on your local machine.
faq.q3: How does the built-in JSON Lint and syntax validator work?
faq.a3: The online JSON parser tokenizes your input in real-time. If it finds a structural error — like a missing bracket, trailing comma, or unexpected token — the JSON lint engine instantly highlights the exact line and describes the issue. It functions as a free JSON lint checker embedded directly in the tool.
faq.q4: Can I use this JSON tool without an active internet connection?
faq.a4: Absolutely. Because the JSON beautifier, compressor, minifier, and free JSON tree viewer are all written in native client-side JavaScript, every feature works perfectly offline once the page is loaded in your browser.
faq.q5: What is the difference between JSON formatting and JSON minifying?
faq.a5: JSON formatting (or pretty printing) adds indentation and line breaks to make JSON data readable. JSON minifying (or JSON compression) does the opposite — it strips all whitespace to produce the smallest possible payload for network transmission. This tool supports both modes, switching instantly in your browser without any server roundtrip.

guide.title: How Base64 Encoding Works
guide.intro: Base64 encoding translates binary data into a set of 64 ASCII characters. Here is how the process works in your browser:
guide.step1: Input Parsing: Plaintext or uploaded files are read into an ArrayBuffer or UTF-8 byte stream using TextEncoder.
guide.step2: Bit Chunking: Data bytes are grouped into 24-bit blocks and divided into four 6-bit index numbers.
guide.step3: Character Lookup: Each 6-bit index maps directly to a character in the RFC 4648 Base64 alphabet.
guide.step4: Padding & Output: Trailing '=' characters are appended as necessary to align 24-bit boundaries.
guide.privacyIntro: Encoding sensitive credentials or certificates with cloud utilities risks data leakage. Local processing ensures full safety:
guide.privacyBullet1: Zero Server Transmission: TextEncoder and Web APIs handle all conversions locally on your machine.
guide.privacyBullet2: URL-Safe Standard Support: Encode tokens for web headers safely without exposing payload values to remote proxies.

faq.q1: What is Base64 encoding used for?
faq.a1: Base64 encoding is primarily used to transmit binary data (like images, zip files, or binary certificates) over network channels that only reliably support text characters, such as embedding media in HTML/CSS Data URIs or passing Basic Authentication credentials in HTTP headers.
faq.a2: No, Base64 is absolutely not encryption. It is a data masking and translation mechanism designed for structural compatibility, not security. Anyone can instantly reverse a Base64 string back to plain text using native tools without any cryptographic keys.
faq.q3: Does this Base64 tool send data to servers?
faq.a3: No. C³ MindLoop handles all text and file string evaluations within your local client device using native browser JavaScript APIs (btoa, atob, and FileReader). Your raw configuration logs, files, and credentials never travel across any public network nodes.

guide.title: How the JWT Inspector & Decoder Works
guide.intro: JSON Web Tokens (JWT) are a compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties. Our interactive JWT Inspector allows backend and frontend developers to debug bearer tokens instantly without sending auth headers across the network.
guide.step1: Paste Authorization Bearer Token: Simply paste your raw JWT string (e.g. eyJhbGci...) into the input editor.
guide.step2: Automatic Structure Separation: The decoder splits the token into its three core dot-separated (.) components: Header (Algorithm & Token Type), Payload (User Claims & Scopes), and Signature Verification.

guide.title: How the Code Complexity Analyzer Works
guide.intro: The analyzer parses your source code entirely in your browser, detects every function and method, and computes two industry-standard complexity metrics per function. Here is the step-by-step process:
guide.step1: Paste or Upload: Paste source code into the input panel or upload a file (.js, .ts, .py, .java, .go, .c, .cpp, .h, .hpp). The language is auto-detected from the file extension or code heuristics.
guide.step2: Click Analyze: The engine scans your code line by line, identifies function boundaries using language-specific patterns, and isolates each function body for independent analysis.
guide.step3: Cyclomatic Complexity: The engine counts every branching construct per function — if, else if, for, while, switch case, catch, &&, ||, and ternary operators. Each adds 1 to the base value of 1.
guide.step4: Cognitive Complexity: Structural constructs (if, for, while, switch, catch) increment the score and add a nesting depth penalty. Deeply nested code penalises more than flat code with the same number of branches.
guide.step5: Risk Classification: Each function receives a risk label — Low, Medium, High, or Critical — based on both scores. Functions at Medium or above receive specific refactor suggestions.
guide.step6: Export Results: Copy results as JSON or download a CSV report for use in code reviews, sprint retrospectives, or CI/CD quality gates.
guide.privacyIntro: Source code often contains proprietary business logic, unreleased algorithms, internal API routes, and secret environment configurations. Uploading it to a cloud-based code analysis service exposes that intellectual property to third-party servers. The C³ MindLoop Code Complexity Analyzer works entirely differently:
guide.privacyBullet1: Zero Transmission: All parsing, metric computation, and report generation executes inside your browser's JavaScript engine. No source code, function names, or analysis results are ever sent to any server or external endpoint.
guide.privacyBullet2: Offline Compatible: Because the analyzer relies entirely on in-memory JavaScript, it continues to produce identical results with no active internet connection. It is safe to use on air-gapped developer machines or in restricted network environments.

faq.a1: Cyclomatic complexity is a software metric that counts the number of linearly independent paths through a function. It starts at 1 and increments by 1 for each branching construct: if, else if, for, while, switch case, catch, logical AND (&&), logical OR (||), and ternary operators. A score of 1–5 is Low risk; 6–10 is Medium; 11–20 is High; above 20 is Critical.
faq.q2: What is cognitive complexity and how is it different from cyclomatic complexity?
faq.a2: Cognitive complexity measures how hard a function is to read and understand, not just how many paths it has. Unlike cyclomatic complexity, it adds a nesting depth penalty — an if statement inside two nested loops scores higher than an if at the top level with the same number of branches. This catches code that is technically not too complex but is genuinely difficult to reason about.
faq.a3: The analyzer supports JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, C, and C++. Language detection is automatic — file extension is used when uploading a file, and code heuristics (keywords, syntax patterns) are used when pasting code. You can always override the detected language manually.
faq.q4: Is my source code uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: No, never. All parsing and metric computation runs entirely inside your browser using JavaScript. Your source code, function names, and analysis results are never transmitted to any server, remote endpoint, or cloud service. The tool works completely offline after the initial page load.
faq.q5: What do the risk levels mean?
faq.a5: Risk levels are derived from both scores using the first matching rule in priority order. Critical means cyclomatic > 20 or cognitive > 24 — the function is extremely complex and should be split. High means cyclomatic > 10 or cognitive > 15 — significant refactoring is recommended. Medium means cyclomatic > 5 or cognitive > 7 — worth reviewing. Low means both scores are within safe bounds.
faq.a6: Suggestions are pattern-specific, not generic. The engine generates: extract deeply nested blocks into helper functions (nesting depth > 3), replace long if/else chains with a lookup table or strategy pattern (more than 4 branches at the same level), extract boolean expressions into named predicate functions (cognitive score > 15 with multiple logical operator sequences), split large functions by responsibility (more than 50 lines), and add unit tests to cover all independent paths (cyclomatic > 10).
faq.q7: Can I sort and export the analysis results?
faq.a7: Yes. The results table can be sorted by Function Name, Cyclomatic score, Cognitive score, or Risk Level by clicking any column header. Results can be exported as a JSON array via the Copy JSON button, or downloaded as a CSV file with the filename pattern complexity-report-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.csv for integration into code review workflows.
faq.q8: How does the analyzer handle nested functions?
faq.a8: Nested functions are detected and scored independently. Decision points belonging to an inner function are not counted toward the outer function's scores. Each function receives its own Function Result with its own cyclomatic score, cognitive score, risk level, and suggestions.
faq.q9: What happens if my code has a syntax error?
faq.a9: The analyzer performs graceful partial analysis. If a syntax error prevents parsing beyond a certain point, results for all successfully parsed functions before the error are still returned and displayed. An inline warning message indicates that the analysis is partial and identifies the error location.
faq.q10: How is this different from linters like ESLint or SonarQube?
faq.a10: Linters enforce code style rules and flag specific patterns. SonarQube performs deep static analysis that requires a build environment and server infrastructure. The C³ MindLoop Code Complexity Analyzer is a lightweight, instant, browser-based tool that focuses specifically on complexity metrics and refactor guidance — no installation, no configuration, no account, and no data leaving your device.

Inline View shows all lines in a single column with removals and insertions interleaved, similar to the output of git diff.
faq.q10: Can I load files from my computer instead of pasting text?
faq.a10: Yes. Each panel has an Upload button that lets you select a plain-text file from your filesystem. The file is read using the browser FileReader API entirely client-side. No file data is transmitted to a server.

editPdf.feat1Desc: Add and position text on any PDF page. Adjust font family, size, colour, and opacity. Double-click any overlay to edit its content inline.
editPdf.feat2Desc: Draw freehand signatures with the signature pad, place images or stamps, and cover existing content with white rectangles. All elements are fully repositionable.

guide.title: How This Works
guide.intro: The PDF Editor lets you annotate, sign, fill forms, and manage pages in any PDF file directly in your browser. Here is the step-by-step workflow:
guide.step1: Upload a PDF: Drop a PDF onto the editor area or click to browse and select a file from your device. The file is loaded entirely in your browser- nothing is uploaded to a server.
guide.step2: Add Text Overlays: Select the Text tool from the toolbar and click anywhere on the page to place a text element. Double-click the element to edit its content. Use the Properties panel on the right to change font, size, colour, and opacity.
guide.step3: Cover Content with Whiteout: Select the Whiteout tool and drag a rectangle over the area you want to cover. This draws an opaque white rectangle that hides underlying content when the PDF is exported.
guide.step4: Place Images or Signatures: Use the Image tool to upload an image from your device and place it on any page. Use the Signature tool to open the signature pad, draw your signature, and position it on the page.
guide.step5: Manage Pages: Use the page thumbnail panel on the left to navigate pages, change their order by dragging, rotate them 90 degrees, or delete pages you do not need in the final document.
guide.step6: Export and Download: Click the Export button in the toolbar to generate the final PDF with all edits embedded using pdf-lib. The file is built in your browser and downloaded directly to your device.
guide.privacyIntro: Uploading sensitive PDF documents to cloud-based editors means your files are transmitted over the network and processed on remote servers. The C³ MindLoop PDF Editor works differently:
guide.privacyBullet1: Client-Side Processing: All editing operations- text overlays, whiteout, image placement, signatures, page management, and form filling- are performed inside your browser using pdf-lib and pdfjs-dist. Your PDF data is processed in local memory and is never sent to any C³ MindLoop server.
guide.privacyBullet2: Suitable for Sensitive Documents: Because processing happens locally, you can safely edit confidential documents- contracts, legal agreements, medical records, or financial statements- without transmitting their contents over the network to a third-party service.

faq.a1: The PDF Editor is a free browser-based tool that lets you annotate, sign, fill forms, and manage pages in any PDF file without installing software. All editing operations run directly in your browser- no file upload to a remote server is required.
faq.q2: Is the PDF Editor free to use?
faq.a2: Yes, the PDF Editor is completely free. There is no account required, no usage limit, and no paid plan. All features including text overlays, whiteout, image placement, signatures, form filling, and page management are available without restriction.
faq.q3: Is my PDF uploaded to a server when I use this tool?
faq.a3: No. The PDF Editor runs entirely inside your browser using pdf-lib and pdfjs-dist. Your PDF file is loaded into browser memory and never transmitted to any server. All editing, rendering, and export operations happen locally on your device.
faq.q4: What editing operations does the PDF Editor support?
faq.a4: The editor supports adding and positioning text overlays with configurable font, size, colour, and opacity; drawing whiteout rectangles to cover existing content; placing images and stamps; drawing freehand signatures; filling AcroForm text fields, checkboxes, and dropdowns; and managing pages by rotating, deleting, or reordering them.
faq.q5: Can I fill in PDF form fields?
faq.a5: Yes. When you load a PDF that contains AcroForm fields, the Properties panel will display the detected fields. You can fill in text fields, toggle checkboxes, and select dropdown values. These values are written into the PDF when you export.
faq.q6: How do I add a signature to a PDF?
faq.a6: Click the Signature button in the toolbar to open the signature pad. Draw your signature using your mouse, touchpad, or touchscreen. Click Confirm to place the signature on the current page. You can then reposition and resize it by dragging.
faq.q7: Can I delete or reorder pages in a PDF?
faq.a7: Yes. The page thumbnail panel on the left side of the editor shows all pages. You can drag thumbnails to reorder pages, click the rotate button to rotate a page, or click the delete button to remove a page from the final document.
faq.a8: Use Ctrl+Z (or Cmd+Z on Mac) to undo the last action, and Ctrl+Y (or Cmd+Shift+Z on Mac) to redo. The undo and redo buttons are also available in the toolbar.
faq.q9: What happens when I export the PDF?
faq.a9: Clicking Export generates a new PDF file that embeds all your edits- text overlays, whiteout rectangles, images, signatures, and form values- using pdf-lib. The file is built entirely in your browser and downloaded directly to your device. The original file is not modified.
faq.q10: Can I use the PDF Editor without installing software?
faq.a10: Yes. The tool runs entirely in your browser using standard web APIs. You do not need to install any application, browser extension, or desktop software. It works in any modern browser on desktop or mobile.

jsonGraphVisualizer.pageTitle: JSON Graph Visualizer- Interactive Node Graph
jsonGraphVisualizer.feat1Desc: Every JSON object and array becomes a draggable node connected by directed edges. Pan, zoom, and click nodes to expand or collapse nested branches.
jsonGraphVisualizer.feat2Desc: An automatic layout engine positions the root node on the left and arranges child nodes progressively to the right, keeping deeply nested structures readable at a glance.
jsonGraphVisualizer.feat3Desc: All graph computation, layout, and PNG export happen entirely in your browser. Your JSON data never leaves your device.

guide.title: How the JSON Graph Visualizer Works
guide.intro: The JSON Graph Visualizer converts any valid JSON document into an interactive node graph where you can explore structure visually, collapse deep branches to reduce noise, and export the result as a PNG image. Here is how it works step by step:
guide.step1: Paste or Load JSON: Paste raw JSON into the left input panel or click Examples to load a pre-built sample. The graph renders automatically within 600ms of your last keystroke.
guide.step2: Explore the Graph: Each JSON object and array becomes a node. Scalar values (strings, numbers, booleans, null) appear as labeled rows inside their parent node. Directed edges connect parent nodes to their child objects and arrays.
guide.step3: Expand and Collapse Nodes: Click any node header to collapse its children and reduce visual complexity. Click again to expand. Collapsed nodes display a badge showing the count of hidden children. Leaf nodes (scalars only) do not respond to clicks.
guide.step4: Pan and Zoom: Scroll with the mouse wheel to zoom, or click-and-drag on empty canvas space to pan. On touch devices, use a two-finger pinch to zoom. The toolbar at the bottom-left provides Zoom In, Zoom Out, and Fit to Screen buttons.
guide.step5: Reset the Layout: Click Reset Layout to restore all nodes to their default collapse state (depth 0 and 1 expanded, depth 2+ collapsed) and re-center the view.
guide.step6: Export as PNG: Click the download icon in the toolbar to capture the full graph canvas- including all nodes and edges, not just the visible viewport- and save it as json-graph.png.
guide.privacyIntro: Unlike cloud-based JSON visualization tools that upload your payload to a remote server for rendering, the C³ MindLoop JSON Graph Visualizer runs the entire pipeline inside your browser:
guide.privacyBullet1: No Data Transmission: JSON parsing, graph construction, layout computation, and SVG rendering all execute in client-side JavaScript. Your API responses, configuration files, and sensitive data structures never leave your machine.
guide.privacyBullet2: Works Offline: Once the page has loaded, the visualizer operates without any internet connection. It is safe to use in air-gapped environments, behind corporate firewalls, or on secured development machines.

faq.q1: What is a JSON Graph Visualizer?
faq.a1: A JSON Graph Visualizer converts a JSON document into an interactive node graph where each object and array is represented as a visual node connected to its children by directed edges. This makes it easy to understand the shape, depth, and relationships within a JSON structure- especially for deeply nested API responses, configuration files, or data schemas- without reading raw text.
faq.q2: How is the JSON Graph Visualizer different from a JSON Tree View?
faq.a2: A tree view displays JSON as collapsible indented text, which works well for shallow structures but becomes hard to follow in wide, deeply nested payloads. The graph view renders each object and array as a spatially positioned node on a zoomable canvas, so you can see the full hierarchy at once, navigate with pan and zoom, and collapse entire subtrees into compact badges. The C³ MindLoop tool offers both views- switch between Graph and Tree using the toggle at the top.
faq.q3: Is my JSON data uploaded to a server?
faq.a3: No. All processing- JSON parsing, graph construction, layout computation, and PNG export- runs entirely inside your browser using client-side JavaScript. Nothing is transmitted to any server. You can safely visualize API keys, database schemas, authentication payloads, or any other sensitive JSON without risk of exposure.
faq.q4: How do I load data into the visualizer?
faq.a4: Paste valid JSON directly into the input panel on the left side of the tool. You can also click the Examples button in the panel header to load one of three pre-built samples: User Profile, API Response, or Config File. The graph or tree renders automatically within 600 milliseconds of your last input change.
faq.q5: What happens when I click a node?
faq.a5: Clicking a node header toggles its collapsed state. When collapsed, all descendant nodes and edges are hidden and a numeric badge appears showing the count of direct hidden children. Clicking again expands the node and restores its immediate children, which retain their own prior collapse state. Nodes that contain only scalar values (leaf nodes) do not respond to clicks.
faq.q6: How large a JSON file can I visualize?
faq.a6: The tool displays a performance warning for payloads with more than 500 keys and automatically skips graph construction for payloads exceeding 2000 keys to protect browser performance. Within those limits, the graph renders the first 200 nodes in breadth-first order and shows a notice if the graph has been truncated. For very large payloads, the Tree View mode is more efficient as it renders on demand.
faq.q7: How do I export the graph as an image?
faq.a7: Click the download icon (Export as PNG) in the graph toolbar at the bottom-left of the canvas. The tool captures the entire graph- all nodes and edges, not just the visible viewport- draws it onto an offscreen canvas with the dark background preserved, and triggers a browser download of json-graph.png. If the canvas is empty, the button is disabled. If export fails due to a browser security restriction, a toast notification will prompt you to use a screenshot instead.
faq.q8: Can I use the JSON Graph Visualizer offline?
faq.a8: Yes. Once the page has loaded in your browser, the visualizer works completely offline. All parsing, layout, and rendering logic is bundled into the page. There are no external API calls, CDN requests, or runtime dependencies that require an internet connection.
faq.q9: What do the colors in the nodes mean?
faq.a9: Node rows use color coding to identify value types at a glance: key labels are rendered in sky blue, string values in emerald green, number values in amber, boolean values in purple, and null values in gray italic. Object and array references show the bracket notation (for example, { … } or [ … ]) to indicate a child node exists connected by an edge.
faq.q10: What is the difference between Graph View and Tree View?
faq.a10: Graph View renders JSON as a zoomable, pannable SVG canvas where objects and arrays are positioned as connected nodes. It is best for exploring structure spatially and understanding relationships between nested objects. Tree View displays the same JSON as a collapsible indented list, similar to a browser DevTools inspector. It is faster for large payloads and better for reading specific values. Both views share the same input panel and respond instantly to changes in the JSON text.
